sections.h2: Visiting the Wake County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The office is in the Wake County Justice Center, 300 S. Salisbury St., Suite 1700, Raleigh, NC 27601. It is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. Call 919-856-5460 or write to rodinfo@wake.gov.

Land documents share the counter with marriage licenses, birth and death certificate copies, business name filings, nuptial agreements and restrictive covenants.

A seller with a Raleigh-area house rarely goes in person. Your closing firm files the deed, and that filing is the step that publishes the sale.

An ordinary deed starts at $26 and a deed of trust at $64, with $4 for each page past the included count.

Large filings pay $2 for each party name beyond twenty, and an assignment's first added deed of trust reference is free.

sections.h2: What counts as a standard deed
sections.html:
Missing any one item on the standard-document list triggers the $25 surcharge. The list covers layout only.

  • Paper sized 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches at the top of the first page, with half-inch margins everywhere else.
  • Black print on white paper in at least 9 point.
  • One side only, with the instrument type centered on page one.

Pen is fine for filling blanks and making corrections. Documents from a title firm pass as a matter of course. A form downloaded and printed double-sided, or a scan that crowds the edge, is the kind of file that draws the extra $25.

The rate is $2 per thousand for deeds since August 1, 1991. State law words it as a dollar per $500 and makes the transferor pay first, so the seller sees it at settlement. Ask the closing office for the number on your deed.

Older rates matter when you read an old transfer: $1 per thousand for 1969 to July 1991 and $1.10 per thousand before 1969.

Wake County public records start in 1785, and the Consolidated Real Property Index lets a seller or a buyer's lawyer follow title from a desk.

Start with your own deed and compare its legal description and owner names against the contract. Next, look for the deed of trust you are paying off. After closing, look for its satisfaction, which is recorded at no charge.

A fraud alert service emails you when a monitored name appears on a recorded document, handy for heirs, landlords and owners of empty houses.

sections.h2: What to have ready before a deed goes in
sections.html:
The package is a signed, acknowledged deed that meets the layout rules, plus payment. Firms handle it for most sellers, but someone recording a family transfer may do it alone.

  • Names written as on the previous deed, since the index is searched by name.
  • Recording fee, plus excise tax if the transfer is a sale.
  • Any added instrument, which carries its own $10 charge when bundled.

For any drafting question, see an attorney. A wrong legal description or missing signature goes back to whoever prepared the deed, and adding or removing an owner means recording a new deed.

sections.h2: The register and the tax office
sections.html:
Two county departments touch the house. The register records the ownership paper, while Tax Administration appraises and bills. Settle the tax bill through closing.

The tax help line is 919-856-5400. Wake also bills towns and special districts, so one bill can carry several charges. The county rate is 53.71 cents after a 2-cent increase for Fiscal Year 2027.

Values reset on January 1, 2027, the effective date of the next revaluation, which sorts about 460,000 parcels into 5,400 neighborhoods.

None of this needs a trip downtown if a closing firm is involved.

  • Your recorded deed, pulled from the online index.
  • The payoff letter for any deed of trust, followed by a recorded release at no charge.
  • A tax figure from Tax Administration, which matters most for owners who pay by escrow and never see a bill.
  • A deed laid out to the standard list.

Heirs unsure what is recorded can search the index, then phone 919-856-5460. An attorney can answer questions about the deed itself.

sections.h2: Services for heirs selling an inherited house
sections.html:
The register sells certified death certificates, which heirs often need for estate paperwork. Certified copies are $10 each, with a $10 amendment charge. For out-of-county death certificates, expect a $14 search fee, a $10 certified copy and $15 for each additional copy. Ordering online adds a county charge of $10 per copy plus a vendor convenience fee that varies.

Certified copies of recorded documents cost $5 for page one and $2 for each page after, with no charge for the trailer page. A certified copy of a map is $5.

  • Get a certified deed copy to show how the decedent held title.
  • Check the index for any open deed of trust before listing the house.
  • Ask an attorney whether probate steps must come before a deed is recorded.

The register does not decide who may sign a deed for an estate. That question belongs to the probate side and to your attorney.

Plats and condominium maps are $21 per page. Right-of-way plans and highway maps are $21 for the first page and $5 for each page after. UCC filings are $38 each for the UCC-1 and UCC-3, rising to $45 above two pages, so a 13-page UCC filing comes to $51.

For a seller, the useful items are the maps and restrictive covenants, since both can describe limits on the parcel. They are recorded here, and the index reaches back to 1785. Ask your title or closing firm to pull any plat and covenant that applies to your subdivision.

Business owners operating from home may also file an assumed name here, at the $26 instrument rate.

Ask the office or your closing firm how a deed will be sent and what cutoff applies. Paper goes to the Justice Center on weekdays. For any question tied to a particular filing, call 919-856-5460 before you go.

sections.h2: Why recording matters after a sale
sections.html:
Until a conveyance is registered in the county where the land lies, it carries no weight against lien creditors or purchasers for value. For a Raleigh-area house, that makes the filing the buyer's protection.

Keep the stamped copy with your closing papers and confirm the old lender's release is recorded. If you sell for cash, the same recording steps apply, only without a lender's paperwork.

sections.h2: Closing-day steps for a Wake County seller
sections.html: Typically the attorney or title firm collects your signed deed, confirms the payoff of any deed of trust, and deducts the excise tax and recording costs from your proceeds. The firm submits the deed, and once it is recorded the index shows the transfer. A week or two later, look the property up and confirm both the new deed and the release of your old loan appear. If either is missing, call 919-856-5460 with the document details.

faqs.q: Is the Wake County deed office open on Saturdays?
faqs.a: No. The Justice Center office keeps weekday hours only. Call 919-856-5460 about holidays.

faqs.q: How is Wake County's deed excise tax stated?
faqs.a: As $2 per thousand on deeds since August 1, 1991. The transferor pays.

faqs.q: Does Wake County charge to record a payoff release?
faqs.a: No. Satisfactions, affidavits of satisfaction and trustee's satisfactions are free.

faqs.q: How do I change the names on a Wake County deed?
faqs.a: With a new deed. The register suggests an attorney unless you are used to preparing legal papers.
